title: quarto-shapes
text: Style divs as shapes that can contain text and other elements. Supports fill, stroke, rotation, and sizing — all composable as classes.

title: quarto-shapes
text:
Installation
quarto add emilhvitfeldt/quarto-shapes

title: quarto-shapes
text:
Quick Start
Add to your YAML front matter:
---
title: My Document
format: html
filters:
  - shapes
---
Then wrap any content in a shape div:
::: {.shape-circle fill="blue"}
Hello
:::

title: quarto-shapes
text:
Typst / PDF output
Shapes also render in Quarto’s typst format (PDF). The existing SVG definitions are embedded as Typst images, so every shape is available. Note these print-specific behaviors.

Size classes map to print lengths: .shape-sm 3cm, .shape-md 5cm, .shape-lg 8cm.
Content is centered within the shape’s bounding box, not its visual outline.

title: quarto-shapes
text:
Modifier classes
Every shape accepts modifier classes. They are fully composable — stack any combination on a single div, in any order:
::: {.shape-hexagon .shape-fill-none .shape-stroke-red .shape-stroke-lg .shape-rotate-90 .shape-md}
:::

Fill — .shape-fill-*
Sets the interior color. Use .shape-fill-none for an outline-only shape (pair it with a stroke).

title: quarto-shapes
text:
Colors, sizes, and modifiers
Colors are set with the fill= and stroke= attributes; size, stroke width, and rotation are classes. Everything is composable — mix attributes and classes on a single div, in any order:
::: {.shape-hexagon fill="none" stroke="red" .shape-stroke-lg .shape-rotate-90 .shape-md}
:::

Fill — fill="…"
Sets the interior color. Accepts any CSS color — a named color (tomato), hex (#3498db), or function (rgb(52 152 219)). Use fill="none" for an outline-only shape (pair it with a stroke).
::: {.shape-circle fill="#3498db"}
:::


Stroke — stroke="…" + .shape-stroke-*
Two independent axes: the outline color comes from the stroke= attribute (any CSS color), and the outline width from a class.

title: Basic Usage
text:
Sizes
Also a modifier, not a shape group — the .shape-{sm,md,lg} classes set the shape’s bounding box. .shape-full fills its container.






For a custom size, use the size= attribute with any length — it overrides the size classes.
